project: Spatiotemporal Air Pollution State Prediction Using Higher-Order Singular Value Decomposition and Kernel Support Vector Machines

fits_completed.stage_b_exact_rbf: Executed on bounded 4k/8k subsets; full-sample 24108 exact RBF omitted due to memory budget (>3.0 GB) and O(N^2) scaling.

test_results_summary.evaluation_scope: Evaluated strictly AFTER freezing LOCKED_SELECTION.json. No test-driven hyperparameter tuning.

planned_not_executed: Full-sample 24108 exact RBF SVC skipped due to compute budget (>3.0 GB resident memory) and O(N^2) scaling; bounded exact subsets (4000 and 8000) and RFF full-sample experiments executed.
limitations: Phase 4 basis transforms were pre-fitted on entire training set; internal calibration folds are not strictly end-to-end forward chaining at the feature extraction level.
PM2.5 class boundary of 75 ug/m3 is a research-defined operational boundary, not an official public health category.
RFF finite-dimensional cosine approximation error exhibits variance across random frequency draws; classification accuracy is not strictly monotonic in D.
Exact RBF SVC at N=8000 vs full-sample N=24108 linear/RFF is not an apples-to-apples sample budget comparison.
honest_conclusions: Unsupervised PCA representations consistently outperform tensor HoSVD representations in linear classification across all dimensions k in {48, 192, 576}. While the Phase 3 Markov baseline achieves 90.75% accuracy by predicting persistence, it detects 0 out of 526 true state transitions. Discriminative SVM and RFF models achieve active transition responsiveness (F1 ~ 0.38, recall ~ 0.50), demonstrating operational utility for dynamic pollution alert systems.
